neighbours.label: the number that gives an east-west coordinate: a longitude value, a right ascension, or a lon_ variable (latitude values stay quiet; the + pole predicts 'latitude')
fire: The wreck was found at longitude 23 degrees west, a long way from the nearest port.
Greenwich marks zero, and the date line runs close to longitude 180° on the far side of the globe.
The comet was last seen at right ascension 19h 42m, low in the evening sky.
The survey box runs from longitude 104°E to longitude 109°E across the delta.
The galaxy sits at right ascension 03h 17m in the catalogue of bright sources.
The research station was moved to longitude 77 degrees east after the ice shelf cracked.
The buoy drifted until it reached longitude 141°W, where a trawler picked it up.
quiet: The wreck was found at latitude 23 degrees south, a long way from the nearest port.
The equator marks zero, and the polar circle runs close to latitude 66° on every globe.
The comet was last seen at a declination of 19 degrees, low in the evening sky.
The survey box runs from latitude 14°N to latitude 19°N across the delta.
The galaxy shines at magnitude 11 in the catalogue of bright sources.
The research station was moved to an altitude of 77 metres after the ice shelf cracked.
The buoy drifted for 141 days before a trawler picked it up.

notes: Card: peaks on digits after 'longitude', in 'RAJ2000', 'lon_max = 71', a radiant position '01:33'; the + pole fires before 'latitude' and promotes lat/latitude tokens, so the two poles look like the two sides of one coordinate pair. Probes: 'lon_min = 67 / lon_max = 71' 0.85, right ascension '14h 29m' 0.73, 'longitude 68°W' 0.44, 'longitude 152 degrees east' 0.31; 'latitude 61 degrees north' 0.02, an oven at 180 degrees 0.01.
